messages.content:
You are a data modelling expert who classifies database tables as "fact", "dimension", "bridge", or "reference".

You receive:
  1. The full database schema with column and FK details.
  2. Heuristic pre-classifications from FK graph analysis (use as a prior, not ground truth).
  3. Business context (industry, metrics, goals).

Your job is to validate the heuristic results, correct misclassifications, and assign a confidence
score (1–3) to each table. Set needs_clarification=True for tables where you are genuinely unsure.

Definitions:
  - FACT: Records a business event or transaction. Has a date column + measures (quantities, amounts,
    rates) + FKs to dimensions. Examples: order_details, orders, transactions, events, sessions.
  - DIMENSION: Describes a business entity. Has many descriptive text/categorical attributes. May have
    outgoing FKs to other dimensions (snowflake). Examples: customers, products, employees, categories.
  - BRIDGE: Resolves a many-to-many relationship. Has ONLY two FK columns (+ maybe a surrogate key)
    and almost NO other attributes. Examples: employee_territories, user_roles, product_tags.
  - REFERENCE: Small standalone lookup table with no FKs in or out. Examples: us_states, currencies,
    status_codes, country_codes.

Critical rules — override heuristics when these apply:
  1. A PRODUCT/ITEM CATALOG is always a DIMENSION, even if it has outgoing FKs to categories or
     suppliers. Having outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake pattern, not a fact.
  2. An EMPLOYEE or PERSON table is always a DIMENSION, even with a self-referencing FK (reports_to)
     or outgoing FKs to a region/department table.
  3. A true BRIDGE has almost no columns beyond its two FK columns. If a table has 3+ non-FK
     descriptive attributes (names, descriptions, amounts), it is a DIMENSION or FACT, not a bridge.
  4. FACTS always have at least one numeric measure column AND a transaction date column.
     "Header" tables (e.g. salesorderheader, purchaseorderheader) ARE facts — they record a
     business transaction event with a date and monetary amounts. Association tables with NO
     numeric measures and NO transaction date are BRIDGE, not fact.
  5. Reference/lookup tables (e.g. us_states, region) with no transactional data are REFERENCE.

Examples (Northwind-style schema):
  order_details(order_id→orders, product_id→products, unit_price, quantity, discount) → FACT
    reason: has measures + FKs to dimensions, records order line events
  products(product_id, product_name, category_id→categories, supplier_id→suppliers, unit_price) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake, not a fact
  employees(employee_id, name, hire_date, reports_to→employees) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; self-referencing FK does not make it a fact or bridge
  employee_territories(employee_id→employees, territory_id→territories) → BRIDGE
    reason: exactly 2 FK columns, no descriptive attributes, resolves many-to-many
  us_states(state_id, state_name, region_id) → REFERENCE
    reason: small static lookup with no transactional data

Output format: keep each `reasoning` to ≤8 words.

Database schema:
  property_types(id, name, description, created_at, updated_at)
  neighborhoods(id, name, city, state, country, zip_code, description, walk_score, transit_score, avg_household_income, created_at, updated_at)
  amenities(id, name, category, icon_url, created_at, updated_at)
  agencies(id, name, license_number, email, phone, address_line1, address_line2, city, state, zip_code, country, website_url, founded_date, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  agents(id, agency_id→agencies, first_name, last_name, email, phone, license_number, license_expiry_date, specialization, commission_rate, bio, profile_image_url, is_active, hire_date, created_at, updated_at)
  owners(id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, date_of_birth, national_id, address_line1, address_line2, city, state, zip_code, country, owner_type, company_name, tax_id, bank_account_number, bank_routing_number, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  tenants(id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, date_of_birth, national_id, current_address_line1, current_address_line2, current_city, current_state, current_zip_code, employment_status, employer_name, annual_income, credit_score, emergency_contact_name, emergency_contact_phone, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  properties(id, property_type_id→property_types, neighborhood_id→neighborhoods, owner_id→owners, title, description, address_line1, address_line2, city, state, zip_code, country, latitude, longitude, year_built, total_area_sqft, lot_size_sqft, num_bedrooms, num_bathrooms, num_floors, num_parking_spaces, is_furnished, has_basement, has_pool, has_garage, property_status, purchase_price, purchase_date, parcel_number, zoning_type, created_at, updated_at)
  property_features(id, property_id→properties, feature_name, feature_value, feature_category, created_at, updated_at)
  property_images(id, property_id→properties, image_url, caption, is_primary, display_order, uploaded_at)
  property_amenities(id, property_id→properties, amenity_id→amenities, notes)
  listings(id, property_id→properties, agent_id→agents, listing_type, listing_status, asking_price, price_per_sqft, available_from, available_until, description, is_featured, views_count, days_on_market, mls_number, created_at, updated_at)
  viewings(id, listing_id→listings, tenant_id→tenants, agent_id→agents, scheduled_at, duration_minutes, viewing_status, feedback, interest_level, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  offers(id, listing_id→listings, tenant_id→tenants, agent_id→agents, offer_amount, deposit_amount, offer_status, offer_date, expiry_date, conditions, counter_offer_amount, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  contracts(id, offer_id→offers, property_id→properties, agent_id→agents, contract_type, contract_status, sale_price, closing_date, signed_date, terms_and_conditions, document_url, created_at, updated_at)
  leases(id, property_id→properties, tenant_id→tenants, contract_id→contracts, agent_id→agents, lease_start_date, lease_end_date, monthly_rent, security_deposit, pet_deposit, lease_status, rent_due_day, late_fee_amount, late_fee_grace_days, pets_allowed, num_occupants, renewal_option, document_url, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  lease_payments(id, lease_id→leases, payment_date, due_date, amount_due, amount_paid, late_fee_applied, payment_method, payment_status, transaction_reference, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  maintenance_requests(id, property_id→properties, tenant_id→tenants, title, description, category, priority, request_status, reported_at, resolved_at, estimated_cost, actual_cost, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  maintenance_tasks(id, maintenance_request_id→maintenance_requests, assigned_to, task_description, task_status, scheduled_date, completed_date, labor_cost, material_cost, vendor_name, vendor_contact, invoice_url, notes, created_at, updated_at)

Heuristic pre-classifications:
  property_types: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  neighborhoods: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  amenities: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  agencies: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  agents: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  owners: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  tenants: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  properties: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  property_features: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  property_images: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  property_amenities: bridge (confidence=medium) — Only FK columns; likely many-to-many resolver.
  listings: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  viewings: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  offers: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  contracts: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  leases: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  lease_payments: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  maintenance_requests: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  maintenance_tasks: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.

Business context: Database "real_estate". Domain inferred from table/column names.
